payload.reason: The evidence provides insights into the criteria used by raters to evaluate classifier outputs, specifically focusing on the appropriateness of predicted error types.

claims.text: Raters selected 'Bad' when the predicted error type did not appropriately characterize the edit, often due to POS or parse errors.
Raters selected 'Good' when the predicted error type was deemed the most appropriate for the edit, while 'Acceptable' indicated it was appropriate but not optimal.
The evaluation was subjective, with raters focusing on the appropriateness of error types despite potential noise from automatic edit extraction.
